tasks.short: Evaluate tool drawings against original form and function requirements

steps.what: Measure drawing dimensions and identify the corresponding original specifications and tolerance references
Compare the selected drawing dimensions with their explicit specification limits
Evaluate tool form and function using the comparisons and record the engineering concerns

tasks.design: Configure a comparison worksheet in {SPREADSHEET} for dimensions the technician has explicitly matched to specifications. Drawing measurement in the design viewer in {OTHER} and evaluation of form and function remain human, with source references held in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated limit arithmetic may sit between dimension measurement and engineering evaluation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas can compare explicit values and limits without deciding whether the tool fulfils its function.
tasks.still_hard: Matching the correct requirements and detecting a design weakness that passes individual dimensions.
tasks.human_edge: The technician understands relationships between geometry, tolerance and tool use.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated comparison arithmetic; no new authority to approve tool design.

reach.task: Provide traceable dimensional and functional concerns

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: explicit dimensional limit comparisons can use configured formulas, while tool form and function evaluation remains human.

assumptions: Boundary covers this drawing evaluation, excluding drawing production and final engineering approval.

OTHER means the mechanical drawing viewer. In s1 the technician produces drawing revision, feature ID, measured value, units, corresponding requirement, lower and upper limits and tolerance interpretation. All measurement, matching and capture remain fully counted.
The machine applies only those matched numerical limits; it does not create a discrepancy code or overall conformity decision. Missing limits or ambiguous geometry require manual evaluation in s3.
Test native comparison or worksheet functions first. Existing calculation runtime earns no saving; added worksheet and method maintenance is counted below.
unknowns: Whether comparison arithmetic is already automatic
The frequency of explicit numerical limits versus functional requirements
research_questions: Can limit arithmetic be removed without shortening measurement, requirement matching or functional evaluation?

already_counted.description: Measure and map dimensions and evaluate form and function

incremental.description: Check unusual tolerance and comparison exceptions
Maintain comparison formulas and accepted methods

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R80 gives gross20, less focal upkeep7 gives net13. Range0-3 assumes most comparisons already use native measurements or formulas and only a few repeated arithmetic operations change; functional evaluation stays full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyse energy requirements and distribution options

steps.what: Define energy requirements, distribution constraints and source-availability cases for the analysis
Calculate and compare energy balances for the selected demand and source scenarios
Analyze scenario results and distribution limitations to recommend energy-use options and further checks

tasks.design: Configure repeat energy-balance scenarios in {SPREADSHEET} from checked requirements and source assumptions documented in {DOCS}. The technician interprets distribution limits and uncertainty and recommends options; the calculation never dispatches generation or changes operating settings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated case calculations can obscure the assumptions driving energy-use comparisons.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formula models can rerun explicit scenarios without inventing availability or physical feasibility.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing credible source profiles and understanding distribution, storage and operating constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The technician can reject an attractive balance that ignores a physical or operational limit.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated scenario arithmetic; operational and investment decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Provide comparable energy scenarios with explicit limitations
reach.learn: Time alignment, balance assumptions and distribution constraints

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: explicit energy-balance scenarios can be calculated deterministically; interpreting feasibility and making recommendations remain human and unmeasured here.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's analysis, excluding metering, plant operation, control changes and investment approval. The quoted source examples are analysed according to their actual operating characteristics, not a presumed category label.

In s1 the technician produces aligned time intervals, demand and generation values, units, source-profile basis, capacity limits, loss assumptions and scenario choices. Checking provenance, capturing fields and reconciling gaps remain fully counted.

Existing metering staff and source operators produce original records outside this analysis task; no saving is claimed in their work. The analysis method owner supplies the accepted calculation method, with added upkeep charged to other_role.

Test native workbook or energy-model configuration first. Missing profiles, inconsistent time bases or unsupported constraints stop automatic calculations and require manual analysis in s3. Existing model runtime is excluded from labour savings.
unknowns: Availability and quality of time-aligned demand and source profiles
Whether repeat scenario arithmetic is already automated
research_questions: Can repeated balance calculations be removed while preserving full review of physical and operating constraints?

already_counted.description: Establish scenario inputs and interpret results and constraints

incremental.description: Investigate scenario exceptions and verify assumption changes
Maintain accepted calculation methods and profile mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R70 gives gross30, less focal upkeep8 gives net22. Range0-5 assumes only a minority of repeat scenarios still need manual arithmetic and constraint interpretation remains unchanged; existing simulation runtime earns no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare parts sketches, work orders and contractor purchase requests

steps.what: Prepare parts sketches and establish the technical scope, quantities and requirements for outside work
outputs: checked parts sketch and request inputs

steps.what: Write work orders and purchase requests using the checked sketch, quantities and scope
inputs: checked parts sketch and request inputs
outputs: work order and purchase request drafts

steps.what: Check technical scope and attachments, then submit the work order and purchase request for approval
inputs: work order and purchase request drafts
checked parts sketch and request inputs
outputs: submitted technical work and purchase request

tasks.design: Configure native work-order and requisition forms in {PROCUREMENT} to reuse the technician's checked scope and sketch references from {DOCS}. The technician checks the draft and submits it into the existing purchasing approval process, without automatically committing spend or contacting a contractor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical facts and attachment references may be retyped into several request forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Native form mappings can reuse explicit request fields while keeping purchasing authority separate.
tasks.still_hard: Defining a scope that a contractor can fulfil without relying on unstated technical assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: The technician can recognise a mismatch between the sketch, requested work and intended outcome.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated request drafting; sketch preparation and spend approval remain unchanged.

reach.task: Provide a complete technical requisition for contractor sourcing
reach.learn: Required request fields and purchasing approval boundaries

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native procurement forms can reuse checked scope fields and attachments; the digest does not measure this contractor-request task.

assumptions: Boundary covers technical sketch and request preparation and internal submission, excluding purchasing approval, supplier selection, contract commitment and contractor work.

OTHER means the mechanical sketching application. In s1 the technician produces part reference, sketch revision, quantities and units, work scope, required outcome, target date, cost centre and attachment references. All sketching, capture and scope judgement remain counted.

The purchasing form owner supplies required field definitions and routing rules, with additional upkeep charged below. No structured approved-supplier or approved-spend flag is assumed. Missing fields or ambiguous scope require manual drafting and checking in s3.
Test native request configuration first. Existing form runtime is excluded. If the sketch is also counted in a detail-drafting task, a roll-up must assign that physical drawing action once.
unknowns: Existing requisition reuse and approval workflow
The proportion of request time spent retyping settled technical facts
research_questions: Can native forms reduce duplicate entry without omitting contractor scope or bypassing purchasing approval?

already_counted.description: Prepare the sketch and technical fields and check and submit the request

incremental.description: Resolve incomplete mappings and check request-template changes
Maintain request forms and approval routing mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact work-order and requisition drafts, technical scope, quantities, sketch revision and attachments checked before internal submission; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R70 gives gross30, less focal upkeep7 gives net23. Range0-5 assumes most request fields already populate and only a minority of duplicated entry changes; sketching and technical checks retain full time.

tasks.short: Assist product tests by setting up instrumentation

steps.what: Assist engineers in product testing by installing, checking and supporting the required instrumentation setup

tasks.design: Keep instrumentation placement, connections and setup verification with the technician under the engineer's test plan in {DOCS}. A stored checklist supports the work but does not install or physically verify instruments.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task involves actual fixtures, sensors, wiring and changing physical test conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's test-recording capability does not remove hands-on instrumentation setup.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting incorrect mounting, damaged connections and a setup that does not represent the test objective.
tasks.human_edge: The technician can inspect and correct the physical installation before the test proceeds.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in physical setup responsibility or test authorisation.

reach.task: Explain instrumentation readiness and unresolved setup concerns
reach.learn: Channel identification, calibration references and setup verification

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: physical test instrumentation setup remains hands-on; no labour reduction for placement and checking is established by the supplied digest.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's product-test assistance and instrumentation setup, excluding test engineering design, test execution by other roles and separate report preparation.

The technician checks sensor identity, placement, orientation, connections, channel mapping, calibration reference and observed setup defects during s1. Capture and physical verification remain fully counted; no free ready-to-test flag is assumed.
Unclear placement, missing calibration evidence or connection discrepancies require manual correction and engineer clarification before proceeding.
Use existing native instrumentation and checklist tools. No new integration or process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Test types and the technician's actual setup and authorisation remit
research_questions: Is any repeated setup transcription separate from the physical installation and verification?

already_counted.description: Install, connect, inspect and support the test instrumentation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives gross0 and net0 with zero upkeep. Routine sensor setup and a complicated crash-test installation both retain full physical work and checking time.
